title: new02; found by us, still unfixed
live_proof: inspection with line numbers in the 3.22.0 tree, and the case is still unfixed upstream: jsonEachColumn()'s default arm returns p->zRoot as SQLITE_STATIC at ext/misc/json1.c:2139, while jsonEachFilter() allocates it at :2244 and jsonEachCursorReset() frees it at :1963. The 3.45.2 fix (28001204f4) converted only the JEACH_JSON arm to SQLITE_TRANSIENT and left this sibling arm as it was
object: p->zRoot, the cursor's own malloc'd copy of the path argument, handed out as SQLITE_STATIC
lifetime_ender: re-filtering the cursor per outer row calls jsonEachCursorReset, which frees the previous zRoot while an accumulator still holds the pointer
fidelity: real consumer, real allocator. Found by us rather than collected: it is the sibling the upstream fix left behind, which is why its upstream_fix is 'unfixed' and not a commit. Same shape and same reduction as case 18; the two differ only in which column of json_each is read

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: CheriBSD 15.0-CURRENT riscv64-purecap, memsys5 over the case's static arena (shared/run-cheribsd.py --mode nested). Revocation acts on a guest malloc free, and under memsys5 there is none: sqlite3_free returns the block to memsys5's own pool inside one array the guest allocator sees as a single live object. So a tag fault here is NOT revocation reporting -- SIGPROT(34) with si_code=2 at the function host ASan reported (fault_sites) is recorded as a catch by the same rule the virtual arms use, and the note says what actually cleared the tag. A fault anywhere else is not tied to the defect

Every SQLite object is one of the guest malloc's, so its end IS a free the quarantine sees and revocation can act. cheribsd-platform.verdict_note: SIGPROT(34) si_code=2 (PROT_CHERI_TAG/untagged-deref) pc=0x40412a98, which is outside jsoneachroot_sys (SharedObject, load base 0x100000) -- the pc is in a shared object and the record does not carry that object's load base, so the faulting function cannot be named from it. This case's declared site is ['binCollFunc', 'memcmp'], a libc routine among them, which is consistent with the fault but not established by it; the run's poscontrol gate FAULTed (exit=162, revocation_default=1) before any case ran The guest has ASLR enabled (kern.elf64.aslr.enable=1), and a shared object's base depends on the library set loaded before it, so the base cannot be reconstructed after the fact either: recording it in the run would be the one change that closes this cell.

fault_sites_why: The min()/max() accumulator keeps the SQLITE_STATIC zRoot pointer and compares against it after jsonEachCursorReset freed it; the comparison is binCollFunc (consumer), whose byte compare is memcmp. Weaker than a single function: any memcmp under this case would count.
